transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get today's project huddle started. As you all know, the school has approved the concept of building a twelve-bed teaching garden beside the science wing, and I have final authority to approve the construction, purchasing, and safety plan. The current draft plan calls for in-ground beds, a volunteer workday on October 18, a $3,000 charge to general funds, and standard latex gardening gloves. Before I can sign off on this campus project plan, I need each of you to report on any requirements you've verified. Let's start with the science teacher -- what can you tell me about the site and any academic requirements?

transcript.text: I need to share something important. I just received soil test results back from the lab yesterday — the soil in the proposed garden area measured lead at 180 parts per million. Our district garden standard requires removing the top six inches of soil and using raised beds at that reading. This came in after the draft plan was circulated, and I haven't entered it into the project folder yet. This means we'll need to revise the plan from in-ground beds to raised beds, and we'll need to account for soil removal as well.
